values.goal: Connect vector coordinates with DOM semantics to build an accessible data map.
values.capstone: A keyboard-editable SVG node map, standalone SVG export, and a report comparing Canvas with the same data

values.title: viewBox and Vectors
values.prerequisites: You should be able to work with JavaScript functions and arrays, DOM events, and coordinates.
values.environment: The existing built-in example provides only a starting point. It does not implement all the extended requirements. Implement this yourself in an HTML and ES module project on a separate local HTTP development server. Record the browser version, viewport, and DPR.
values.concepts.0.title: User coordinates
values.concepts.0.explanation: viewBox defines the internal coordinate range. Changing the screen size does not change the shape data itself.
values.concepts.1.title: Preserving proportions
values.concepts.1.explanation: preserveAspectRatio determines how the internal rectangle fits the viewport. meet and slice produce different padding or clipping.
values.outcomes.0: Distinguish internal coordinates from screen size.
values.outcomes.1: Explain differences in position and thickness when resizing.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-01.js and index.html in an external practice project. Create a 300×150 badge in inline svg using rect,circle,path.
values.steps.1: Change viewBox and preserveAspectRatio with a select, and display the screen size and internal coordinates.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the input condition 0 0 300 150, then run again with 0 0 600 300. Compare the hypothesis, "Shapes at the same coordinates appear smaller on screen," against the display and logs, and record the actual result and the causes of any differences in day-01-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: viewBox
values.variables.0.expected: Shapes at the same coordinates appear smaller on screen
values.criteria.0: Distinguish internal coordinates from screen size.
values.criteria.1: Explain differences in position and thickness when resizing.
values.questions.0: Does changing viewBox also change the path data?
values.questions.1: Which can clip a shape, meet or slice?
values.references.0.title: MDN SVG from Scratch Tutorial

values.prerequisites: Prerequisite concepts: Paint and input, Bubbling. Prepare the result files and observation records from Unit 16.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes preparation for extending the assignment in a separate project. Implement this yourself in an HTML and ES module project on a separate local HTTP development server. Record the browser version, viewport, and DPR.
values.concepts.0.title: Drag offset
values.concepts.0.explanation: Saving the difference between the pointer and node center prevents a jump at the start. Calculate coordinates in the same user space.
values.concepts.1.title: Cancellation path
values.concepts.1.explanation: pointercancel may differ from normal completion. Group capture release and temporary state cleanup in a shared function.
values.outcomes.0: Dragging ends even when released outside the region.
values.outcomes.1: Movement has the correct ratio even while zoomed in.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-17.js and index.html in an external practice project. On pointerdown, save the difference between inverse-matrix coordinates and the node position, and capture the pointer.
values.steps.1: Update transform on pointermove and finish on pointerup and pointercancel.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the input condition Node center, then run again with Node edge. Compare the hypothesis, "Keeping the offset prevents the node from jumping," against the display and logs, and record the actual result and the causes of any differences in day-17-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: Starting position
values.variables.0.expected: Keeping the offset prevents the node from jumping
values.criteria.0: Dragging ends even when released outside the region.
values.criteria.1: Movement has the correct ratio even while zoomed in.
values.questions.0: How do you handle drag state when pointerId changes?

values.title: Zooming and Panning
values.prerequisites: Prerequisite concepts: Drag offset, Cancellation path. Prepare the result files and observation records from Unit 17.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes preparation for extending the assignment in a separate project. Implement this yourself in an HTML and ES module project on a separate local HTTP development server. Record the browser version, viewport, and DPR.
values.concepts.0.title: Camera group
values.concepts.0.explanation: Transforming the content group moves the entire map. Keep on-screen controls outside the group to preserve their size.
values.concepts.1.title: Pointer-centered zoom
values.concepts.1.explanation: For natural zooming, the same local point must stay at the same screen position before and after zooming. Changing only scale makes the graphic jump toward the origin.
values.outcomes.0: The node of interest does not jump during zooming.
values.outcomes.1: Provide minimum and maximum scales and a reset button.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-18.js and index.html in an external practice project. Manage translate and scale of the content g as state.
values.steps.1: For zoom buttons and wheel input, calculate the local point under the pointer and compensate for translation.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the input condition Origin, then run again with Pointer position. Compare the hypothesis, "The node under the pointer stays at the same screen point after zooming," against the display and logs, and record the actual result and the causes of any differences in day-18-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: Zoom center
values.variables.0.expected: The node under the pointer stays at the same screen point after zooming
values.criteria.0: The node of interest does not jump during zooming.
values.criteria.1: Provide minimum and maximum scales and a reset button.
values.questions.0: What happens if you put on-screen controls in the content group?
values.questions.1: How do you distinguish wheel page scrolling from zooming?

values.title: Data and DOM Updates
values.prerequisites: Prerequisite concepts: Camera group, Pointer-centered zoom. Prepare the result files and observation records from Unit 18.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes preparation for extending the assignment in a separate project. values.concepts.0.title: Stable ids
values.concepts.0.explanation: A data id connects a DOM element to its data. It identifies the same object even when array order changes.
values.concepts.1.title: Incremental updates
values.concepts.1.explanation: Replacing all innerHTML may lose focus and event connections. Updating only necessary attributes and elements makes state easier to preserve.
values.outcomes.0: The selected id does not change after reordering.
values.outcomes.1: Clean up DOM and Map references for deleted ids.

values.steps.1: Reorder the data, remove one node, and record whether selection and focus persist.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the input condition Full replacement, then run again with id-based attribute updates. Compare the hypothesis, "Unchanged elements retain their identity and focus," against the display and logs, and record the actual result and the causes of any differences in day-19-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: Update method
values.variables.0.expected: Unchanged elements retain their identity and focus
values.criteria.0: The selected id does not change after reordering.
values.criteria.1: Clean up DOM and Map references for deleted ids.
values.questions.0: How do you handle the same id arriving twice?

values.title: Connectors and Graph Layout
values.prerequisites: Prerequisite concepts: Stable ids, Incremental updates. Prepare the result files and observation records from Unit 19.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes preparation for extending the assignment in a separate project. Implement this yourself in an HTML and ES module project on a separate local HTTP development server. Record the browser version, viewport, and DPR.
values.concepts.0.title: Derived paths
values.concepts.0.explanation: Connectors are data calculated from the coordinates of two nodes. Storing them separately may leave stale coordinates after movement.
values.concepts.1.title: Layer order
values.concepts.1.explanation: SVG draws in document order. Placing connectors first displays them beneath nodes and labels.
values.outcomes.0: Reject edges that reference missing nodes.
values.outcomes.1: Connector endpoints match after moving a node.
values.steps.0: Prepare day-20.js and index.html in an external practice project. Build a small learning map with a node array and an edge array using sourceId,targetId.
values.steps.1: Update path d from both endpoints on every drag, and place the connector group before the nodes.
values.steps.2: Save the output under the input condition Fixed, then run again with Move one node by 80 units. Compare the hypothesis, "Only paths connected to that node point toward its new position," against the display and logs, and record the actual result and the causes of any differences in day-20-notes.md.
values.variables.0.name: Node position
values.variables.0.expected: Only paths connected to that node point toward its new position
values.criteria.0: Reject edges that reference missing nodes.
values.criteria.1: Connector endpoints match after moving a node.
values.questions.0: Why calculate connector coordinates instead of storing them?
values.questions.1: Does changing layer order also affect selection?

values.concepts.0.title: Interpolation
values.concepts.0.explanation: Calculating between start and end values using a time ratio can smooth movement. Using frame count makes speed depend on refresh rate.
values.concepts.1.title: Motion preference
values.concepts.1.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion signals a preference for less unnecessary movement. State changes must also be communicated without animation.
values.outcomes.0: Information remains even with animation disabled.
values.outcomes.1: Clean up previous frame requests when transitions overlap.
